q: Which city hall became the world's tallest building in 1901, ushering in the secular-skyscraper era?
ref: History of Architecture Tables, p. 22 — Timeline of Tallest Skyscrapers (World)
n: Philadelphia City Hall, at 167 meters, took the title in 1901 and held it until 1908, when the Singer Building surpassed it.

q: Which hospital-affiliated dormitory did Mapua design?
ref: History of Architecture Tables, p. 22 — Filipino Architects: Mapua, Tomas Bautista
n: Mapua designed the Philippine General Hospital Nurses Home, housing nursing staff at the government hospital in Manila.

q: Besides Quezon City, Santos-Viola's Franciscan churches also rose in Singalong, Mandaluyong, Tagaytay, and which other city?
ref: History of Architecture Tables, p. 22 — Filipino Architects: Santos-Viola, Carlos Antonio
n: His Franciscan commissions extended to Lipa City, alongside Singalong, Mandaluyong, and Tagaytay.

q: The Woolworth Building held the world's-tallest title from 1913 until which year?
ref: History of Architecture Tables, p. 22 — Timeline of Tallest Skyscrapers (World)
n: The Woolworth Building's 17-year reign lasted until 1930, when the Bank of Manhattan Trust Building briefly overtook it.

q: At about 112.5 meters, which building was the country's tallest between 1989 and 1991?
ref: History of Architecture Tables, p. 22 — Timeline of Tallest Buildings (Philippines)
n: The Pacific Star Building, with 29 floors, held the tallest-building title from 1989 to 1991, before The Peak Tower surpassed it.

q: Sindiong's international work includes a rice research institute in which country?
ref: History of Architecture Tables, p. 22 — Filipino Architects: Sindiong, Antonio S.
n: He designed the East Pakistan Rice Research Institute in Bangladesh, alongside a housing project in Indonesia and villas in the UAE.

q: Which building held the world's-tallest title for the longest single stretch on this timeline, about 41 years?
ref: History of Architecture Tables, p. 22 — Timeline of Tallest Skyscrapers (World)
n: The Empire State Building held the record from 1931 to 1972, the longest reign of any building on this timeline.

q: Which building surpassed the Rufino Pacific Tower as the country's tallest in 1997?
ref: History of Architecture Tables, p. 22 — Timeline of Tallest Buildings (Philippines)
n: The Robinsons Equitable Tower took the title in 1997, reaching 175 meters across 45 floors, before Petron Megaplaza overtook it the following year.

q: Toledo also designed which teacher-training institution?
ref: History of Architecture Tables, p. 22 — Filipino Architects: Toledo, Antonio Manalac
n: Toledo designed the Philippine Normal School. St. La Salle Hall and the Mapúa Institute trace to Tomas Bautista Mapua, and the UST Main Building to Roque Ruano.

q: The Sears Tower, tallest from 1974 to 1998, is located in which city?
ref: History of Architecture Tables, p. 22 — Timeline of Tallest Skyscrapers (World)
n: The Sears Tower in Chicago held the title for 24 years, the second-longest reign on this timeline after the Empire State Building.

q: Which building was the Philippines' tallest from 2000 until 2017?
ref: History of Architecture Tables, p. 22 — Timeline of Tallest Buildings (Philippines)
n: The PBCom Tower, at 259 meters and 52 floors, held the title for 17 years, the longest reign since the Manila Hotel, until the Grand Hyatt Manila overtook it in 2017.

q: Which government department building, later tied to tourism, did Toledo design?
ref: History of Architecture Tables, p. 22 — Filipino Architects: Toledo, Antonio Manalac
n: Toledo designed the Department of Agriculture and Commerce building, later associated with the Department of Tourism. He separately designed the Department of Finance building.

q: The Burj Khalifa, the current world's tallest building, surpassed Taipei 101 with a height increase of roughly what percentage?
ref: History of Architecture Tables, p. 22 — Timeline of Tallest Skyscrapers (World)
n: At 828 meters, the Burj Khalifa was about 62.61% taller than Taipei 101, by far the largest jump of any transition on this timeline.

q: How many floors does Horizons 101 Tower 1 in Cebu City have?
ref: History of Architecture Tables, p. 22 — Timeline of Tallest Buildings (Philippines)
n: Horizons 101 Tower 1 rises 185 meters across 55 floors, taller than every Metro Manila building until the PBCom Tower and Grand Hyatt Manila.

q: Which Pasig office towers are credited to Villarosa?
ref: History of Architecture Tables, p. 22 — Filipino Architects: Villarosa, Rogelio Garcia
n: Villarosa designed Tektite Towers in Pasig. The other three towers belong to Metro Manila's later tallest-building timeline, not his portfolio.

q: Roxas's Jesuit Church of Sa Ignacio stands in which historic walled district of Manila?
ref: History of Architecture Tables, p. 22 — Filipino Architects: Roxas, Felix Arroyo
n: Sa Ignacio is inside Intramuros, Manila's old walled city. Ermita, Quiapo, and Malate are other historic Manila districts tied to different architects' projects on this list.

q: What height did the Rufino Pacific Tower reach?
ref: History of Architecture Tables, p. 22 — Timeline of Tallest Buildings (Philippines)
n: The Rufino Pacific Tower reached 162 meters across 41 floors, holding the title from 1994 to 1997.

q: Jose Maria Zaragosa designed the headquarters of which utility company?
ref: History of Architecture Tables, p. 22 — Filipino Architects: Zaragosa, Jose Maria
n: Zaragosa designed the Meralco Building in Pasig. PLDT, Petron, and San Miguel are other major Philippine companies not tied to this project.

q: Ruano designed a Filipino Catholic church as far away as which country?
ref: History of Architecture Tables, p. 22 — Filipino Architects: Ruano, Roque
n: His Santa Teresita Church stands in Yokohama, Japan. Sindiong, not Ruano, is linked to projects in Malaysia, Indonesia, and the UAE.

q: Which building's 1890 completion produced the largest single percentage jump in height among these early titleholders, at about 137%?
ref: History of Architecture Tables, p. 22 — Timeline of Tallest Skyscrapers (World)
n: The New York World Building more than doubled the previous record, jumping from 42 to 94 meters, a leap unmatched by any other transition on this timeline except the Burj Khalifa's.

q: Which Makati church is credited to Zaragosa?
ref: History of Architecture Tables, p. 22 — Filipino Architects: Zaragosa, Jose Maria
n: Zaragosa designed Union Church in Makati. St. John Bosco and Pius XII Catholic Center are his other church projects, but located elsewhere.

q: Which recreational club is credited to Idelfonso Paez Santos?
ref: History of Architecture Tables, p. 22 — Filipino Architects: Santos, Idelfonso Paez
n: Santos designed the Raintree Sports Club in Kuala Lumpur, Malaysia. The Makati Sports Club, Puerto Azul clubhouse, and Araneta Center Cubao all belong to Rogelio Garcia Villarosa's body of work.

q: The Park Row Building, tallest from 1899 to 1901, reached what height?
ref: History of Architecture Tables, p. 22 — Timeline of Tallest Skyscrapers (World)
n: Park Row Building reached 119 meters, the last titleholder before the record passed to a purely secular skyscraper era in 1901.

q: Which De La Salle building did Mapua design?
ref: History of Architecture Tables, p. 22 — Filipino Architects: Mapua, Tomas Bautista
n: Mapua designed St. La Salle Hall at De La Salle University. The UST Main Building, UP Padre Faura campus, and Manila City Hall belong to other architects.

q: Which Quezon City church is credited to Santos-Viola?
ref: History of Architecture Tables, p. 22 — Filipino Architects: Santos-Viola, Carlos Antonio
n: Santos-Viola designed Our Lady of Lourdes Church in Quezon City. The other three churches were all designed by Jose Maria Zaragosa.

q: The Singer Building overtook Philadelphia City Hall in 1908 with a height increase of about how much?
ref: History of Architecture Tables, p. 22 — Timeline of Tallest Skyscrapers (World)
n: The Singer Building rose to about 186.57 meters, an 11.72% increase over Philadelphia City Hall, before the Metropolitan Life Tower surpassed it the next year.

q: Which building held the Philippines' tallest-building title the longest, from 1912 to 1967?
ref: History of Architecture Tables, p. 22 — Timeline of Tallest Buildings (Philippines)
n: The Manila Hotel, with 18 floors, held the title for 55 years, far longer than any of its successors, before the postwar building boom began overtaking it.

q: Antonio S. Sindiong designed a major shopping mall in which city?
ref: History of Architecture Tables, p. 22 — Filipino Architects: Sindiong, Antonio S.
n: His SM Megamall project rose in Mandaluyong. He also designed Harrison Plaza in Manila and Ali Mall II and New Farmers Plaza in Cubao.

q: Which building held the world's-tallest title only briefly in 1930, before the Chrysler Building surpassed it?
ref: History of Architecture Tables, p. 22 — Timeline of Tallest Skyscrapers (World)
n: The Bank of Manhattan Trust Building held the record for less than a year in 1930 before the Chrysler Building took over in 1931.

q: The Peak Tower held the tallest-building title for roughly how long?
ref: History of Architecture Tables, p. 22 — Timeline of Tallest Buildings (Philippines)
n: The Peak Tower's reign lasted only from 1991 to 1992 before the Pacific Plaza Condominium overtook it, one of the shortest stretches on this timeline.

q: Which housing project abroad is credited to Sindiong?
ref: History of Architecture Tables, p. 22 — Filipino Architects: Sindiong, Antonio S.
n: Sindiong designed the Kebayoran Housing Project in Indonesia. The other three options are Rogelio Garcia Villarosa's works.

q: The Empire State Building's 1931 height increase over the Chrysler Building was about what percentage?
ref: History of Architecture Tables, p. 22 — Timeline of Tallest Skyscrapers (World)
n: At 381 meters, the Empire State Building was about 19.1% taller than the Chrysler Building, one of the larger jumps on this timeline.

q: Which two consecutive titleholders both had exactly 45 floors, despite differing in height?
o: PBCom Tower and Grand Hyatt Manila
Pacific Plaza Condominium and Rufino Pacific Tower
The Peak Tower and Pacific Star Building
Robinsons Equitable Tower and Petron Megaplaza
ref: History of Architecture Tables, p. 22 — Timeline of Tallest Buildings (Philippines)
n: Robinsons Equitable Tower (175 m) and Petron Megaplaza (210 m) both had 45 floors, showing floor count doesn't always track height directly, since ceiling heights and floor plans vary between buildings.

q: Which University of the Philippines site is credited to Toledo?
ref: History of Architecture Tables, p. 22 — Filipino Architects: Toledo, Antonio Manalac
n: Toledo designed the UP Padre Faura campus, UP's original Manila home before the Diliman campus was built.

q: Petronas Towers took the world's-tallest title in 1998 with the smallest recorded height increase on this timeline, at about what percentage?
ref: History of Architecture Tables, p. 22 — Timeline of Tallest Skyscrapers (World)
n: At 451.9 meters, Petronas Towers was only 2.24% taller than the Sears Tower, the narrowest margin of any transition on this timeline.

q: At 318 meters and 66 floors, which building has held the country's tallest-building title since 2017?
ref: History of Architecture Tables, p. 22 — Timeline of Tallest Buildings (Philippines)
n: The Grand Hyatt Manila has held the title since 2017, currently the tallest building in the Philippines.

q: Rogelio Garcia Villarosa designed which five-star hotel along EDSA?
ref: History of Architecture Tables, p. 22 — Filipino Architects: Villarosa, Rogelio Garcia
n: Villarosa designed the Edsa Shangri-la Hotel. The Manila Pavilion Hotel, Grand Hyatt Manila, and Silahis International Hotel are unrelated to his portfolio here.

q: In which city does the Burj Khalifa, the current world's tallest building, stand?
ref: History of Architecture Tables, p. 22 — Timeline of Tallest Skyscrapers (World)
n: The Burj Khalifa stands in Dubai, UAE, and has held the world's-tallest title since 2010.

q: How many floors does the current tallest building in the Philippines, Grand Hyatt Manila, have?
ref: History of Architecture Tables, p. 22 — Timeline of Tallest Buildings (Philippines)
n: Grand Hyatt Manila has 66 floors, the highest floor count on this entire timeline.

q: Villarosa designed a hotel along which historic Manila boulevard?
ref: History of Architecture Tables, p. 22 — Filipino Architects: Villarosa, Rogelio Garcia
n: His Silahis International Hotel sits along Roxas Boulevard. Taft Avenue, España, and Quezon Avenue are other major Manila thoroughfares unrelated to this project.

q: Roque Ruano is best known for which university landmark?
ref: History of Architecture Tables, p. 22 — Filipino Architects: Ruano, Roque
n: Ruano designed the UST Main Building along with several religious and collegiate structures, such as Dominican House in Baguio. St. La Salle Hall went to Tomas Bautista Mapua, UP Padre Faura to Antonio Manalac Toledo, and Manila City Hall also to Toledo.

q: Which building held the tallest-skyscraper title first, from 1870 to 1884, though it was still shorter than the tallest cathedral of its day?
ref: History of Architecture Tables, p. 22 — Timeline of Tallest Skyscrapers (World)
n: The Equitable Life Building, at 40 meters, was the first tallest-skyscraper titleholder, but church spires of the era still stood taller overall.

q: Which Quezon City church and convent did Zaragosa design?
ref: History of Architecture Tables, p. 22 — Filipino Architects: Zaragosa, Jose Maria
n: Zaragosa designed the Santo Domingo Church and Convent in Quezon City. The other three churches belong to Carlos Antonio Santos-Viola's work.

q: Ruano's "Crucero" addition belongs to the Church of Our Lady of Manaoag, in which province?
ref: History of Architecture Tables, p. 22 — Filipino Architects: Ruano, Roque
n: Manaoag, home to the shrine church, is in Pangasinan. Cavite, Batangas, and Laguna are linked instead to other architects' projects here.

q: The Manhattan Life Insurance Building, at 100 meters, held the tallest title for about how long?
ref: History of Architecture Tables, p. 22 — Timeline of Tallest Skyscrapers (World)
n: Its reign lasted only from 1894 to 1895 before the Milwaukee City Hall surpassed it, one of the shortest stretches on this timeline.

q: Zaragosa's Pius XII Catholic Center rose along which avenue?
ref: History of Architecture Tables, p. 22 — Filipino Architects: Zaragosa, Jose Maria
n: The Pius XII Catholic Center stands along UN Avenue in Manila.

q: Santos designed a public plaza in which Cavite town?
ref: History of Architecture Tables, p. 22 — Filipino Architects: Santos, Idelfonso Paez
n: The Imus Town Plaza in Imus, Cavite is among his projects. Bacoor is instead tied to Felix Arroyo Roxas's parish church work.

q: Starting in 1901, the record for world's tallest building has always belonged to what kind of structure?
ref: History of Architecture Tables, p. 22 — Timeline of Tallest Skyscrapers (World)
n: From 1901 onward, every titleholder has been a secular skyscraper, ending the earlier era when tallest-skyscraper titleholders still stood shorter than the tallest churches and cathedrals.

q: Mapua designed Librada Avelino Hall for which school?
ref: History of Architecture Tables, p. 22 — Filipino Architects: Mapua, Tomas Bautista
n: Librada Avelino Hall was designed for Centro Escolar University, named after the school's founder.

q: Santos-Viola's Nuestra Senora de Guia church stands in which Manila district?
ref: History of Architecture Tables, p. 22 — Filipino Architects: Santos-Viola, Carlos Antonio
n: Nuestra Senora de Guia is in Ermita, Manila. Intramuros is instead linked to Felix Arroyo Roxas's Jesuit church.

q: Which tower, built for a life insurance company, was the world's tallest from 1909 to 1913?
ref: History of Architecture Tables, p. 22 — Timeline of Tallest Skyscrapers (World)
n: The Metropolitan Life Tower held the title for four years before the Woolworth Building surpassed it in 1913.

q: Which building briefly took the title from the Manila Hotel before losing it to the Manila Pavilion Hotel the following year?
ref: History of Architecture Tables, p. 22 — Timeline of Tallest Buildings (Philippines)
n: The Ramon Magsaysay Center held the title only from 1967 to 1968, a short reign before the Manila Pavilion Hotel took over.

q: Which shopping center in Manila did Sindiong design?
ref: History of Architecture Tables, p. 22 — Filipino Architects: Sindiong, Antonio S.
n: Sindiong designed the Harrison Plaza Shopping Center in Manila. The other three options belong to Rogelio Garcia Villarosa's portfolio.

q: The Chrysler Building, tallest from 1930 to 1931, reached approximately what height in feet?
ref: History of Architecture Tables, p. 22 — Timeline of Tallest Skyscrapers (World)
n: The Chrysler Building reached about 1,050 feet (319.9 meters), a 13.04% increase over the Bank of Manhattan Trust Building, before the Empire State Building overtook it the following year.

q: Which condominium briefly stood as the Philippines' tallest building from 1992 to 1994?
ref: History of Architecture Tables, p. 22 — Timeline of Tallest Buildings (Philippines)
n: The Pacific Plaza Condominium, at 150 meters and 44 floors, held the title until the Rufino Pacific Tower surpassed it in 1994.

q: Antonio Manalac Toledo designed the seat of Manila's city government. What is it called?
ref: History of Architecture Tables, p. 22 — Filipino Architects: Toledo, Antonio Manalac
n: Toledo, who served as Manila's city architect, designed Manila City Hall. The other options are hotels and a later office tower unrelated to his body of work.

q: Which building took the world's-tallest title from the Empire State Building in 1972?
ref: History of Architecture Tables, p. 22 — Timeline of Tallest Skyscrapers (World)
n: The World Trade Center in New York held the title from 1972 to 1974, before the Sears Tower in Chicago overtook it.

q: Petron Megaplaza, at 210 meters, became the country's tallest building starting in which year?
ref: History of Architecture Tables, p. 22 — Timeline of Tallest Buildings (Philippines)
n: Petron Megaplaza held the title from 1998 to 2000, when the PBCom Tower surpassed it.

q: Toledo designed a provincial capitol in which province?
ref: History of Architecture Tables, p. 22 — Filipino Architects: Toledo, Antonio Manalac
n: Toledo designed the Leyte Capitol. Cebu, Bohol, and Samar are neighboring provinces not tied to this project.

q: Which building held the world's-tallest title from 2003 to 2010, standing about 509 meters?
ref: History of Architecture Tables, p. 22 — Timeline of Tallest Skyscrapers (World)
n: Taipei 101 held the title for seven years before the Burj Khalifa surpassed it by a wide margin in 2010.

q: Which building on this timeline stands not in Metro Manila but in Cebu City?
ref: History of Architecture Tables, p. 22 — Timeline of Tallest Buildings (Philippines)
n: Horizons 101 Tower 1, completed in 2016, is the tallest building outside Metro Manila, which is why it sits apart from the main Metro Manila lineage on this timeline.

q: Villarosa's Alexandra project in Pasig is notable for being what kind of development?
ref: History of Architecture Tables, p. 22 — Filipino Architects: Villarosa, Rogelio Garcia
n: Alexandra is an 11-building residential complex in Pasig, one of Villarosa's larger-scale projects.

q: Which architect handled the enlargement and reconstruction of the parish church in Bacoor, Cavite?
ref: History of Architecture Tables, p. 22 — Filipino Architects: Roxas, Felix Arroyo
n: Felix Arroyo Roxas took on the Bacoor parish church project; he's also credited with the Jesuit Church of Sa Ignacio in Intramuros. Ruano, Santos, and Toledo are other Filipino architects known for separate landmark works.

q: The Manila Pavilion Hotel, at 90 meters with 22 floors, reigned as the country's tallest building for roughly how many years?
ref: History of Architecture Tables, p. 22 — Timeline of Tallest Buildings (Philippines)
n: The Manila Pavilion Hotel's 21-year reign from 1968 to 1989 was the second-longest on this timeline, behind only the Manila Hotel.

q: Which Villarosa project is located in Pasong Tamo?
ref: History of Architecture Tables, p. 22 — Filipino Architects: Villarosa, Rogelio Garcia
n: King's Court II sits in Pasong Tamo. Araneta Center is in Cubao, and the Puerto Azul clubhouse is a resort project, both separate Villarosa works.

q: Which of the following was NOT designed by Roque Ruano?
ref: History of Architecture Tables, p. 22 — Filipino Architects: Ruano, Roque
n: Ruano's projects include Dominican College, Santa Catalina College, and the Hospital of the Sacred Heart. Manila City Hall belongs to Antonio Manalac Toledo, who served as Manila's city architect.

q: The Home Insurance Building, widely regarded as an early skyscraper landmark, stood in which city?
ref: History of Architecture Tables, p. 22 — Timeline of Tallest Skyscrapers (World)
n: The Home Insurance Building rose in Chicago and held the tallest-skyscraper title from 1884 to 1890, a modest 6.15% taller than the Equitable Life Building before it.

q: Zaragosa's Philippine Airlines building rose along which avenue?
ref: History of Architecture Tables, p. 22 — Filipino Architects: Zaragosa, Jose Maria
n: The Philippine Airlines building stands along Ayala Avenue, Makati's main business thoroughfare.

q: Idelfonso Paez Santos designed a memorial park located in which city?
ref: History of Architecture Tables, p. 22 — Filipino Architects: Santos, Idelfonso Paez
n: His Eternal Gardens Memorial Park is in Manila. Santos also handled leisure projects such as the Batulao Village Club in Batangas and Caliraya Lake Resort in Laguna.

q: Which building outside New York or Chicago briefly became the world's tallest, as a city hall, in the 1890s?
ref: History of Architecture Tables, p. 22 — Timeline of Tallest Skyscrapers (World)
n: Milwaukee City Hall held the world's-tallest title from 1895 to 1899, an unusual stretch when a city hall outside the two dominant American skyscraper cities took the record.

q: Tomas Bautista Mapua designed the main postal building in which Manila district?
ref: History of Architecture Tables, p. 22 — Filipino Architects: Mapua, Tomas Bautista
n: The Manila Central Post Office Building stands in Ermita. Mapua, the first registered Filipino architect, later founded what is now Mapúa University.

q: Carlos Antonio Santos-Viola served as chief architect for the church structures of which organization?
ref: History of Architecture Tables, p. 22 — Filipino Architects: Santos-Viola, Carlos Antonio
n: Santos-Viola was chief architect for Iglesia ni Cristo, including its Templo Central. The Union Church of Manila, by contrast, was designed by Jose Maria Zaragosa.
